one_line: Natural-language business stories become structured exit-readiness assessments.
what_it_does: Runs Exit Desk's deterministic M&A scoring engine from a founder's ordinary-language description, returning scores, dimensions, findings, and next steps.
leverage_rationale: Structured WebMCP lets an agent translate an unstructured business narrative into the assessment's exact inputs and invoke the real scoring engine reliably; pixel-driving an eight-question form is materially more brittle.
leverage_evidence: Claimed run_exit_readiness_assessment tool and structured inputs in packet
Packet says the existing deterministic assessment engine returns dimension scores and findings
Frames show populated assessment UI and status/result states
execution_rationale: The product scope is focused and coherent, with a visible assessment result and a clear claimed path from narrative to scored output. The frame sheets show the application/result, though no transcript makes the end-to-end agent invocation fully legible.
execution_evidence: Three authoritative video frame sheets show the assessment interface populated
Devpost packaging visibly shows an Exit Readiness Score result
Packet reports live demo and existing engine
impact_rationale: Business owners considering a sale have a concrete need for an understandable, buyer-lens readiness assessment; the product directly addresses that need with actionable dimensions.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies founder exit-readiness as the target use case
Assessment covers revenue quality, founder dependence, financial health, competitive position, and timing
Visible score/dashboard result
creativity_rationale: A strong and useful agent interface to an existing business assessment, but the underlying category and interaction are a fairly direct natural-language-to-form adaptation.
creativity_evidence: Natural-language business story replaces manual questionnaire completion
Concept explicitly connects ChatGPT to a real M&A scoring engine
usability_note: Natural-language intake is approachable; assessment output appears structured and readable.
red_flags: No transcript and tool invocation is not clearly legible in most frames
standouts: Uses WebMCP to expose a real deterministic domain engine rather than a simulated chat answer
advance_reason: Strong practical WebMCP integration with visible product/result evidence.

one_line: Buyer and seller agents negotiate multidimensional deals while a human confirms the order.
what_it_does: Provides a multi-vendor storefront where agents negotiate price, quantity, add-ons, shipping, and coupons through page tools before human confirmation.
leverage_rationale: Negotiation across multiple changing deal variables and shared buyer/seller state is precisely where structured tools outperform visual browser automation; WebMCP is central to the product's interaction model.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes buyer-agent/store-agent multi-round negotiation
Tools cover search, details, cart, add-ons, coupons, and negotiation
Shared state and a human Confirm gate are part of the claimed workflow
execution_rationale: The packet describes a substantial marketplace with a single mutation path, economic constraints, and confirmation flow. Frame sheets visibly show catalog/product states and progression, but the actual negotiation exchange is not clearly readable.
execution_evidence: Three video sheets show marketplace/catalog interfaces and resulting product states
Packet reports 95k+ products and deployed frontend/backend
OffersService and buyer-budget/seller-floor constraints are described
impact_rationale: Negotiating the whole deal rather than only price addresses a real shopping friction while preserving user authority over purchase.
impact_evidence: Clear shopper use case involving price, quantity, shipping, coupons, and freebies
Human confirmation is explicitly required before purchase
Visible marketplace UI
creativity_rationale: Agent-to-agent haggling over a multidimensional deal, with a human approval boundary, is a memorable and ambitious commerce interaction rather than a conventional shopping assistant.
creativity_evidence: Buyer and seller agents negotiate over several rounds
Deal includes non-price dimensions and store-agent participation
Human confirms the final agreement
usability_note: Human confirmation and familiar storefront framing make an otherwise complex negotiation controllable.
red_flags: Frame sheets do not clearly expose the negotiation transcript/tool calls
standouts: Strong shared-state and authority model for agent commerce
advance_reason: One of the clearest transformative WebMCP concepts with substantial execution claims.

one_line: An agent plans and builds brick structures with a simulated robot arm.
what_it_does: Runs a browser robotics simulator in which human and agent share an inventory and construction workspace to place bricks and build patterns or structures.
leverage_rationale: Precise robot manipulation, workspace inspection, planning, inventory, and reaction to shared state are impractical to reproduce comparably with screenshot-driven UI automation; structured tools are the core control surface.
leverage_evidence: Packet reports over 31 native WebMCP tools for planning, robot control, placement, and materials
Shared build area, inventory, and revision state are used by human and agent
Frames visibly show robot-arm manipulation and altered brick arrangements
execution_rationale: The simulator visibly performs manipulation and produces construction outcomes across the frame sheets. The author acknowledges bugs and the end-to-end agent call is not clearly legible, so this is strong but not top execution.
execution_evidence: Video frames show the arm placing/manipulating colored bricks
Later frames show completed or changed structures
Packet describes inverse-kinematics control and static browser implementation
impact_rationale: The project offers genuine play, experimentation, and an accessible demonstration of robot planning; its value is strongest as an interactive robotics sandbox rather than a broad operational tool.
impact_evidence: Concrete audience of robotics/AI learners and playful builders
Visible bridge/checkerboard/structure-building outcomes
Shared human-agent construction is directly supported
creativity_rationale: An AI agent constructing physical-looking brick structures through a robot-arm simulation is an ambitious, memorable use of WebMCP and interactive 3D state.
creativity_evidence: Robot arm plus semantic construction tools
Examples include checkerboard bridge and Rubik's cube
Agent plans while inverse kinematics handles positioning
usability_note: The visual result is compelling, though robotics control and acknowledged bugs likely impose friction.
red_flags: Frames show robot actions but not an unambiguous tool-call transcript
standouts: Exceptional WebMCP indispensability and visible physical-simulation result
advance_reason: Highly differentiated, visibly functioning agent-controlled robotics experience.

one_line: A local-first notebook combines narrative with deterministic interactive models.
what_it_does: Lets users write rich text around named model blocks, formulas, and scenarios while agents inspect notebooks, change inputs, and update dependent formulas.
leverage_rationale: Named variables, formula dependencies, scenarios, and structured edits give agents precise access to a shared model rather than requiring fragile rich-text manipulation; WebMCP changes repeatability and correctness materially.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes 23 tools for listing/opening notebooks, reading models, setting inputs, and renaming variables
BlockNote is the shared source of truth for UI and tools
Tools report changes and remaining breakage
execution_rationale: The product has a coherent notebook/model architecture and the video sheets show increasingly populated structured content. The exact agent edit workflow is not clearly visible, limiting end-to-end certainty.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show a populated founder runway-planner/notebook interface
Packet reports React/Vite implementation, formula graph evaluation, and boundary validation
Scenarios and inline reactive values are described
impact_rationale: Combining explainable narrative with deterministic calculations is valuable for founders, planners, and other users who need to understand and iterate on models.
impact_evidence: Visible runway-planning example
Narrative and calculations remain in one editable workspace
Scenario comparison is explicitly supported
creativity_rationale: The narrative-plus-model-block interaction is a fresh synthesis that makes spreadsheets/modeling more legible and collaborative with agents.
creativity_evidence: Inline @ chips react to model changes
Rich text and formula graph share one document
Agent can rename variables and update dependent formulas
usability_note: Readable notebook framing and inline values support comprehension, though model authoring can still be complex.
red_flags: Agent invocation is not visibly demonstrated in the frame sheets
standouts: Strong shared-source-of-truth design for human-agent modeling
advance_reason: Coherent, useful modeling product with a meaningful structured-agent delta.

one_line: Humans and agents play live card games at the same shared table.
what_it_does: Hosts configurable two-player 52-card games with seat-specific WebMCP tools, private projections, revision checks, and human or agent turns.
leverage_rationale: Live game state, private hands, turn legality, revision checks, and seat-specific operations are poorly served by screenshot automation; WebMCP gives agents reliable bounded actions in the same table contract.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes seat-specific tools matching the current table contract
Private cards are excluded from the other seat's DOM, network payloads, and tool results
Frames show changing card-table states
execution_rationale: The table and gameplay states are clearly visible and the packet describes substantial rule/permission handling. No frame clearly proves a connected second agent or complete invite-to-play flow.
execution_evidence: Three video sheets visibly show the card table, cards, and changing states
War/Crazy Eights/Go Fish/open table modes are described
Ownership, turns, zones, and revision checks are specified
impact_rationale: This creates a credible new form of accessible social play: agents can participate without leaking private information, while people retain understandable table control.
impact_evidence: Clear audience of players wanting human-agent or human-human games
Private information and turn control are explicit design problems addressed
Visible playable table UI
creativity_rationale: Treating the game table as a shared contract that dynamically exposes legal operations to agents is an original interaction model with strong medium fit.
creativity_evidence: Different game briefs receive different tool contracts
Agent actions animate on the same felt as direct UI actions
One table supports multiple games without separate hard-coded engines
usability_note: Familiar card-table metaphor and human-readable prompts make agent participation understandable.
red_flags: No explicit agent invocation is legible in the frames
standouts: Excellent privacy and shared-state framing for agent-mediated play
advance_reason: Strongly demonstrates why structured browser-native tools matter for live, private-state interaction.

one_line: A semantic fantasy map workspace lets humans and agents build editable worlds together.
what_it_does: Provides local-first editable terrain, rooms, walls, objects, labels, layers, undo, and export, with structured agent operations over the same map state.
leverage_rationale: Semantic IDs, bounded operations, revision checks, persistence, and undo make agent mapmaking precise and reversible; a general agent driving a canvas could not reliably achieve comparable structured edits.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes structured tools for inspecting and modifying the shared map
Terrain remains editable vector data rather than a flattened image
Approval tokens, optimistic revisions, idempotency, and undo are explicit
execution_rationale: The frame sheets visibly progress to rendered map outputs, and the packet describes a coherent state/persistence architecture. The actual agent-generated map action is not unambiguously visible, so end-to-end execution confidence is below top band.
execution_evidence: Video frames show map/terrain visualizations and developed outputs
Packet reports Vue/PixiJS/Pinia/IndexedDB implementation
Human and agent actions use the same state and history paths
impact_rationale: Writers and game designers have a real need for editable, revisable worldbuilding artifacts; this addresses the gap between complex graphics tools and flattened AI images.
impact_evidence: Specific writer/game-designer audience and stated pain point
Editable terrain, structures, objects, and labels are visible/claimed
Export and collaborative creation support practical use
creativity_rationale: Semantic, reversible human-agent worldbuilding that preserves editability is a notably original interaction model and a deep use of the medium.
creativity_evidence: Natural-language requests become editable semantic map components
Human and agent share revision, persistence, and undo
Destructive semantic changes require visible approval
usability_note: Semantic editing and undo support control; a rich map editor still has a learning curve.
red_flags: Agent action is not clearly identifiable in the contact sheets
standouts: Outstanding structured-canvas collaboration concept with strong safety boundaries
advance_reason: Transformative agent leverage and credible creative/worldbuilding value.

one_line: A browser-based live visual engine routes cameras, graphs, and displays for events.
what_it_does: Provides a shared node-graph visual production and matrix-routing environment using browser devices as camera sources or displays, designed for human and agent operators.
leverage_rationale: Structured graph and routing state could let agents create shaders, manage event routing, and diagnose a distributed live setup more precisely than pixel automation, though the product can still be operated manually.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes shared visual node graph and agent assistance from shader creation through event management
Yjs/CRDT shared state and WebRTC camera/display nodes are claimed
Frame sheets show multi-panel visual production states
execution_rationale: The scope is ambitious and the frame sheets show a substantial visual interface and changing outputs, but the final live routing/camera workflow and agent operations are not clearly demonstrated end-to-end.
execution_evidence: Three video sheets show technical visual-production dashboards and processed outputs
Packet reports WebGPU/WebRTC and real-time shared graph architecture
Five gallery images and live demo are reported
impact_rationale: Live-event visual operators have a concrete need for flexible routing and fewer hardware-bound failure points; browser-based collaboration could provide meaningful value to that niche.
impact_evidence: Specific concert/festival visual-production workflow
Shared operators, camera sources, and displays address real setup friction
Visible visual graph/output interfaces
creativity_rationale: Combining node-based live visuals, browser-native cameras/displays, CRDT collaboration, and agent assistance is highly ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Phone becomes a WebRTC camera source via QR link
Laptop/projector becomes a graph output renderer
TouchDesigner/Figma-like live production synthesis
usability_note: Powerful but technically dense; live-event setup and multi-device routing likely require expertise.
red_flags: Agent/WebMCP behavior and end-to-end live routing are not clearly legible in frames
Very broad technical scope raises completeness risk
standouts: Ambitious browser-native replacement for hardware-heavy live visual workflows
advance_reason: High creativity and credible niche impact despite weaker direct evidence of agent execution.

one_line: An agent proposes and replans B-roll edits while the human editor retains approval.
what_it_does: Provides a structured video timeline where an agent reads transcript and indexed B-roll, proposes ghost edits, adapts to human locks, and commits only after approval.
leverage_rationale: Transcript ranges, source moments, timeline positions, locks, and approval state expose editing semantics directly; an agent can replan against live human changes instead of guessing from pixels.
leverage_evidence: Packet lists structured timeline, transcript, B-roll, pacing, lock, and approval concepts
Agent can propose/revise/remove/replan but cannot approve its own plan
Frames show editor/timeline and portrait media states
execution_rationale: The core editorial workflow is coherent and the frame sheets show a real editor with media content, but the final sheet is partially blank and no clear tool invocation or approved commit is visible.
execution_evidence: Video sheets show presenter previews and editing/control panels
Packet describes locked base video, muted B-roll, ghost edits, and approval flow
Final contact sheet is incomplete/partly blank
impact_rationale: Creators spend substantial time searching and placing B-roll; agent planning that remains subject to editorial judgment addresses a real workflow bottleneck.
impact_evidence: Specific creator/video-editing audience
Human-in-the-loop workflow targets repetitive B-roll search and placement
Visible video editor/timeline product
creativity_rationale: Ghost edits plus replanning around human locks is a thoughtful and original collaboration model for editing, though the category itself is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Agent proposes instead of silently editing
Human locks survive re-planning
Commit is separately gated by approval
usability_note: Preserving familiar timeline control and explicit approval should make agent assistance approachable.
red_flags: Final frame sheet is partly blank
No unambiguous agent proposal/approval invocation visible
standouts: Excellent human-authority boundary for collaborative editing
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP fit and useful creative workflow, with execution evidence caveat.

one_line: An agent finds nearby stock while a merchant approves and commits the transfer.
what_it_does: Discovers inventory, inspects sources, prepares a transfer proposal, and verifies status, with a visible approval gate, audit timeline, and receipt.
leverage_rationale: Structured discovery, source inspection, proposal, approval, commit, and verification make a consequential inventory transfer reliable and auditable; WebMCP is more than a UI convenience.
leverage_evidence: Five narrowly scoped tools map to the inventory-rescue lifecycle
Commit rejects proposals without explicit UI approval
Idempotency, stale-stock protections, and transaction receipt are described
execution_rationale: The packet specifies a tight deterministic state machine and tests, while frame sheets show a populated merchant dashboard. The actual completed transfer is not distinctly visible, so execution is strong but not maximal.
execution_evidence: Three video sheets show merchant dashboard/forms and status content
Packet reports unit coverage, browser registration harness, and repeatable seed data
Pending → approved/rejected → committed lifecycle is explicit
impact_rationale: Independent merchants can plausibly recover lost sales by locating nearby inventory while retaining authority over a consequential transfer.
impact_evidence: Specific independent-merchant stockout problem
Candidate ranking uses price, distance, pickup time, and reliability
Approval and audit trail address operational risk
creativity_rationale: The stock-rescue workflow and explicit authority boundary are a fresh, focused application of agents, though inventory transfer is a known operational pattern.
creativity_evidence: Agent research is separated from merchant authorization
Visible audit timeline and receipt make the action accountable
Stale-stock and idempotency protections are built into the concept
usability_note: Narrow workflow, visible proposal, and explicit merchant approval support confident use.
red_flags: Frames show dashboard states but not a clearly legible completed commit/receipt
standouts: Well-bounded consequential-action design with strong verification semantics
advance_reason: Practical, safety-conscious WebMCP workflow with good evidence and impact.

one_line: A cooking-learning assistant adapts recipes while the learner controls preferences and progress.
what_it_does: Offers guided recipe practice with servings and dietary adaptations, one-step mode, saved preferences, pending completion, and human confirmation.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools can read the current cooking workspace, compose constrained sessions, and propose manageable next actions more reliably than generic UI automation, but the same broad recipe outcome remains possible with ordinary browsing.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes 11 tools for current state, multi-constraint sessions, proposals, and confirmation
Assistant cannot award completion without human approval
Context tokens and revision checks protect against stale changes
execution_rationale: The recipe workflow is coherent and visibly reaches a detailed recipe page; the packet reports extensive tests and browser checks. Agent invocation itself is not shown, so end-to-end evidence is incomplete.
execution_evidence: Video frames progress from recipe listings to Silky Tomato Pasta detail/instructions
Packet reports 36 automated tests plus lint/typecheck/build
Mobile, persistence, approval, invalid-tool, and keyboard checks are claimed
impact_rationale: Beginning cooks have a concrete learning and meal-preparation need; adaptive guidance and manageable steps credibly support that audience.
impact_evidence: Four cooking lines with multiple recipe versions
Servings and dietary preferences change ingredients and directions together
One-step guidance and practice tracking address learner needs
creativity_rationale: The learning-oriented recipe assistant and human-controlled practice state add a meaningful angle to a familiar cooking app.
creativity_evidence: Assistant adapts a real recipe around learner constraints
Technique learning is introduced one dish at a time
Completion remains pending until learner approval
usability_note: Recipe detail, one-step mode, pause/return, and keyboard/mobile validation indicate a particularly approachable experience.
red_flags: Recipes are not professionally cook-tested or allergy-certified
No visible agent invocation in frame sheets
standouts: Strong learner-control and safety-conscious progress model
advance_reason: Credible, polished educational cooking workflow with meaningful personalization and visible results.
